notes:
Summary of account and open threads:
- Customer: enterprise LegalTech search provider; heavy regulatory constraints (data residency + audit).
- Current infra: Elastic for retrieval + on-prem BERT-based reranker; costs high at scale, slow tail latency spikes.
- Scale: ~120M docs, 10-20k daily updates; expected peak 200 QPS.
- Target: p95 end-to-end <250ms; reduce cost-per-query to <$0.005 while keeping MRR within 1-2% of baseline.
- Migration approach requested: evals-driven embedding + reranker migration. They want held-out evaluation sets, automatic regression alerts, and ability to run A/B and canary rollouts with traffic splitting.
- Specific asks from SE call:
  * Example eval suite (MRR, MAP, recall@k) for legal queries (provided by customer).
  * Guidance on embedding model selection & quantization tradeoffs for 120M index.
  * Cost modeling for indexing (one-time embed computation + incremental updates) and per-query cost including reranker.
  * Implementation patterns: hybrid retrieval (sparse + dense), prefix caching, cold/warm shard strategy for on-prem dedicated pools.
- Security: Must integrate with customer KMS, SAML SSO, full audit logs for every query and rerank decision. Data residency: EU subset needs to stay in eu region for certain clients.
- Risks noted: embedding/reranker quality regressions during model swaps; they expect Redwood Optimize + evals to provide regression guards and automated rollback.
- Next steps agreed: Redwood to provide a POC plan (2-week A/B canary) with: sample cost estimate, infra diagram for dedicated/private deployment, eval harness + baseline metrics, and a list of compatibility considerations for their on-prem infra.
- Internal follow-ups: escalated to infra team for estimated GPU footprint; RINF-1134 opened to track quantized kernel support for their model family.
Quotes/Customer lines: "We need to be 95% confident that a new reranker won't regress MRR more than 1% — otherwise legal ops pushes back."
